openings.claim: Reconcile batches through a row-preserving ledger and supported alternative replacement identities, depending on recorded supersession, dictionary meaning and cutoff applicability instead of recency or quantity equality. Preserve duplicates and unmatched rows; use only U=5V and supplied status aggregation meanings; never infer missing quantities from neighboring batches. Differently identified older replacements remain distinct without supplied identity evidence.
openings.discriminator: Against a conservative explicit-reference-only rival, supported interpretations can resolve quantities invariant across interpretations and expose disagreement when replacement identity changes results. Additional resolutions may be zero; equal converted quantities never establish identity.
openings.probe: Within twenty extra minutes, compare both spreadsheet/local-script variants on clean and disturbed copies, each with the same sixty-minute review cap. Allocate minutes 0-15 to capture/conversion, 15-40 to amendment/cutoff checks, 40-60 to decisions/requests. Freeze twelve batch decisions and citations, with at most three requests naming the missing superseded-row reference, undefined status dictionary entry, and, if needed, record linking differently identified replacements. Open the sealed key afterward; compare resolved-batch, unsupported-definite-claim and request counts. Inspect invariant survival after reference removal and undefined status.
openings.uncertainty: Exhaustive interpretation feasibility within sixty minutes remains uncertain. Unsupported identity links, missed surviving rows or enumeration beyond reviewer capacity defeat the approach. Stop enumeration and report bounded disagreement; the cap alone gives no evidence of informativeness. At the deadline cite candidate quantities and unresolved fields; undefined status cannot support a definite total. Further uncertainty remains reported beyond three requests.
